checklist.area: Recovery input discard and consent/Force drain semantics
checklist.evidence: R10-S1: src/tui.rs:1286 and :1322 treat a false zero-time event poll as a fully drained input boundary. vendor/crossterm/src/event/read.rs:65–90 can return false after one filtered internal terminal reply while parsed application events remain queued. Recovery can consequently classify old shortcuts as fresh, and presentation can advance with an old confirmation still queued.

R10-S2: vendor/crossterm/src/event/source/unix/mio.rs:107–136 loops over a ready TTY without checking the requested deadline or imposing a work/byte bound when parsing produces no complete event. The outer elapsed check cannot bound this inner loop.

checklist.area: Inherited blocking descriptors and parent-shell flags
checklist.evidence: The patched vendor/crossterm/src/event/source/unix/mio.rs uses a zero-time level-readiness check before revisiting the potentially blocking borrowed TTY. It does not apply F_SETFL/O_NONBLOCK to shared parent-shell descriptors. vendor/crossterm/src/terminal/sys/unix.rs retains raw-mode restoration rather than changing parent open-file flags.

findings.title: A filtered zero-time poll is incorrectly used as a recovery and consent drain
findings.impact: Queued pre-recovery native shortcuts can survive the recovery fence and be interpreted as deliberate fresh control requests. The same false-drain predicate can promote a painted Force warning to Confirmable or submit conditional consent while previously queued human input remains pending. This undermines fresh-human-provenance and no-replay guarantees; it is separate from historical unknown PTY application settlement.
findings.evidence: vendor/crossterm/src/event/read.rs:65–90 reads one source event, filters CursorPosition/KeyboardEnhancementFlags/PrimaryDeviceAttributes out through EventFilter, then returns false because the zero-duration deadline has elapsed—even when UnixInternalEventSource.parser still contains subsequent application events. The patched mio source returns the next parsed internal event first at lines 73–75. At src/tui.rs:1285–1304, two such false polls suffice to end the recovery drain and its final pending-input check; line 1315 clears drain_recovered_input. Thus terminal replies followed by an already queued control shortcut can cross that boundary. src/tui.rs:1322–1325 also calls authority.after_draw on the same false result; src/tui/control.rs:1261–1311 then promotes ForcePresentation::Drawn to Confirmable and queues eligible consent, and :1105–1115 accepts Enter as a Force claim. [INFERENCE from static control flow] An outer-input stream containing enough filtered terminal replies ahead of a queued shortcut/Enter can satisfy these checks without the queued human event being drained. Existing tests check ordinary queued keys, not this interleaving.
findings.fix: Do not equate the filtered public poll(false) result with an empty input boundary. Implement a bounded, explicit drain/readiness operation that inspects all already buffered source events and pending TTY input, continues past filtered terminal replies, and distinguishes genuinely empty from deadline/work-budget exhaustion. Keep recovery and consent/Force presentation fenced on an inconclusive result. Add regression coverage with terminal replies preceding queued control shortcuts and prepaint Enter, verifying no fresh claim, consent, or Force admission.

findings.title: Ready TTY input can bypass the native reader deadline indefinitely
findings.impact: The explicitly required bounded native input-reader contract is not met. A continuously ready incomplete terminal sequence can monopolize an event::poll call, preventing the TUI from reaching its pause/disconnect checks, bounded recovery drain, safe-quit handling, or later resize tokens. This is an input-side availability/boundedness defect, not a claim that provider output can execute host commands.
findings.evidence: The elapsed-time check at mio.rs:84 runs only outside processing the retained readiness batch. Inside TTY_TOKEN, lines 107–136 repeatedly perform zero-time readiness, read, and parse; there is no elapsed check or byte/work cap if parser.next returns None. Parser::advance at :213–231 retains incomplete sequences. vendor/crossterm/src/event/sys/unix/parse.rs:813–821 returns None for an unterminated bracketed paste, regardless of how much content has accumulated. [INFERENCE from static control flow] A terminal-input producer that keeps such a paste/sequence ready can therefore keep the inner loop running beyond a finite or zero requested timeout; the caller's 1024-event bound is ineffective because no complete event is returned. The level-readiness check avoids an ordinary idle blocking read but does not bound this work.
findings.fix: Bound work within each TTY readiness visit and honor the caller deadline even when parsing produces no event. Retain the current readiness token/parser state when yielding so unread edge-triggered input is not lost; make budget exhaustion distinguishable from a proven empty drain so it cannot recreate R10-S1. Preserve parent-shell descriptor flags. Add source-level regression cases for finite/zero polls on sustained incomplete input, subsequent resize/wakeup progress, and safe recovery behavior.

summary: FAIL: 23 of 25 checklist items passed; score = 100 × 23/25 = 92. Reviewed all 92 frozen paths and narrow unchanged authority references. Two supported Should-fix source-integration findings remain: filtered zero-time polling is not a valid human-input drain, and the patched TTY reader lacks an inner-loop bound. Neither finding waives or repackages historical unknown native application settlement. No optional considerations are reported.
limits: Read-only static source review only. No edits, shell/source execution, builds, tests, lint, formatting, network/provider calls, daemon/config/auth operations, payload execution, commits, or independent hash/Git verification were performed. Actual auth/private inputs, retired private fixtures, previous reviews/audits, runtime reports, saved handoff/state, execution logs, and PLAN.md after line 45 were not consulted. Released-source identity and baseline provenance were taken from the sealed manifest; inactive/release-identical vendor files received integration/surface review, not a fresh upstream certification. Source assertions and deterministic fixtures do not establish installed OMP same-instance live acceptance, provider approval, runtime cleanup, or native application settlement. Findings describe statically derived paths, not observed exploit executions.
